fields.description: Sage VIP Premier only has 2 payrolls per Frappe Company (Monthly/Salaried employees are on one, Hourly/Wage employees on the other) - Senior/Executive Management sit outside both and are never part of a Sage-sourced pull.
fields.label: Payroll Type

fields.description: Sage's own top-level tenant code (e.g. "A3T" for Isambane, "XCA" for Excavo) - informational only, not used in the batch import file itself.
fields.label: Sage Group Code

fields.description: Sage's 3-digit Company Number for this payroll (e.g. "001") - written zero-padded as the CoNo field of every line in the generated .txt, and used to name the Windows-host ODBC DSN this payroll's employee data is pulled from ("VIP_Company" + this value).
fields.label: Sage Company Number

fields.description: 1-character batch number/letter (1-9 or A-Z), written as the BatNo field of every line in the generated .txt.
fields.label: Batch Number

fields.description: Every Sage Paypoint that rolls up into this Company Number, and the Branch each maps to. sage_employee_puller.py (the Windows-host bridge script) queries Sage once per Paypoint listed here; is_attendance.controllers.sage_payroll.ingest_employees() uses this same mapping to resolve each pulled employee's Branch.
fields.label: Paypoints

fields.options: What each of the 6 generic amount columns in Sage's batch import format holds, for this payroll - matches the flexible column choice the original VBA batch-import tool prompted for interactively, pre-configured here instead. Only the values proven this session (worked hours + the 3 leave-hour buckets) are offered - allowance/baseline columns aren't included because no evidence was found of them being sourced live from Sage; add them here once a real source is confirmed.
